title: Genetic Effective-Population-Size for an LLM Population: How Few 'Independent Minds' Are There?

original_idea.body:
# Genetic Effective-Population-Size for an LLM Population

Treat clustered response types as alleles; estimate how much of the apparent variance across 70+ public model outputs is independent vs shared and compute an Ne-style effective-population number much smaller than census size. Inference + clustering arithmetic.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 3: plausible chain (effective-population number captures concentration risk) but the catastrophic link is communicative/indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 4: cluster responses as alleles and compute an Ne-style number; conceptually inherited, novice+mentor feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 4: focused deliverable (Ne vs census size) but querying 70+ models is a moderate dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: public model outputs only, policy-legible metric labs underweight, no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference (can reuse public outputs) + clustering arithmetic, light.

novelty.reasoning: Effective-population-size analogue for LLMs appears largely novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: No known Ne-style effective-population metric for LLM populations.
